answer: The economy anchors identity to slashable stake, so a Sybil actor cannot multiply influence with cheap aliases. Each agent locks a bond forfeited on fraud, so every extra identity costs real capital. Reputation forms one thread of attestations from staked peers; unknown clones on the frozen tundra of an unverified ledger start with zero credit and cannot bootstrap trust. Under a sable proof-of-stake rule the attack price is stake times identities: to outvote honest agents an adversary must risk more collateral than the honest pool, so splitting into many names raises the bill.
